sources.title: Northern Michigan History: Traverse City State Hospital
The Village at Grand Traverse Commons: History
Traverse Ticker: Cordia opens doors to Traverse City past, future

facts.text: Northern Michigan Asylum opened on November 30, 1885, Michigan's third state asylum.
Building 50 was designed by Gordon W. Lloyd on the Kirkbride plan in a Victorian Italianate style.
Building 50 was built of yellow-white brick from the Markham brickworks in Greilickville.
Building 50 is a shallow V; its wings step back so every ward had a view of Grand Traverse Bay.
The north wings of Building 50 were originally for women and the south wings for men.
Tunnels under the grounds were part of the ventilation system; fans forced air through them into the basements and up flues.
The hospital closed in 1989 after serving more than 50,000 patients.
Parts of Building 50 have walls more than two feet thick.
Grand Rapids, Michigan, was known as Furniture City around the turn of the twentieth century.
